Lessons.Title: How Would You Describe These Figures?
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will motivate the need for geometric language for describing and drawing images and to introduce points, lines, and segments.
In earlier grades, you examined, described, compared, and contrasted attributes of two-dimensional figures. You may have used geometric terms such as point , line , and segment intuitively and informally. This lesson serves two goals.

2021 lesson activities: Warm-up: Notice and Wonder: String Art (5 minutes); Activity 1: Do You See What I See? (25 minutes); Activity 2: Lines and Line Segments (15 minutes); Cool-down: Lines and More (5 minutes)
Corrected mathematical focus: A point marks a location; a straight line extends without endpoints, while a segment has exactly two endpoints.

Edulytics authored guidance: Look at the original string-art figure, then identify visible points. Describe which marks are full straight lines and which are finite segments. On a dot field draw five lines through pairs of points and explain the labels.
First-party Cool-down (not publisher assessment): Draw line AB and segment CD through labelled points; explain which has endpoints.
Images, drawing/protractor accuracy, partner tasks and the gated original publisher Cool-down require original task evidence and teacher/visual review.
